dhana-nidhanaya.method: Fair-balls prior over the balls in use, plus three evidence sources in the owner's order. A jackpot-winning combination counts as 12 draws, acting only through its decades, odd/even mix, spread and letter, with 2 average pseudo-jackpots added. A jackpot-winning date counts as 4 draws, through draws held on calendar-similar days (moon phase, day of month, weekday; fitted on this lottery's own dates; contrast with ordinary days). A daily draw counts as 1. Each lower source is damped to at most 75% of the pull of the source above it, and no number's lean leaves 0.75-1.25. Cards follow copy, typicality and diversity rules. Walk-forward backtest over the last 200 draws, or fewer so that each replayed draw has at least 30 earlier draws, using only evidence known before each draw.
dhana-nidhanaya.disclaimer: Lottery draws are random and every combination is equally likely. These picks are a statistical curiosity for entertainment only; they do not improve your odds. Please play responsibly.

calendar.peak: about 2 days before the full moon

text.verdict: Over the last 178 Dhana Nidhanaya draws, using only what was known before each draw, the Top pick matched 0.163 numbers per draw. A random ticket matches 0.195, and the previous model matched 0.174. That is the same as random; the difference is luck (95% range -0.094 to +0.030). Across all 5 lotteries (934 draws): 0.1863 vs 0.2042.
text.power: With 178 draws, only an effect of about +57% or more would show up reliably in this test (in 4 cases out of 5), after allowing for the 7 checks made for this lottery.
text.copyTilt: The Top pick held on average 0.21 numbers from past jackpots; a random ticket holds 0.40. The model leans toward the tens where jackpot numbers fell, and never repeats two numbers of the same jackpot.

explanation.summary: All balls start equal; three kinds of evidence then move the picks, strongest first. Share of the pull on the numbers today: Jackpot combinations 54% · Jackpot dates 26% · Daily draws 20%.
explanation.weights: A jackpot combination counts like 12 draws, a jackpot date like 4, a daily draw like 1. Daily draws are turned down so they never outweigh the dates.
explanation.combinations: 3 jackpot combinations, used only through their tens, odd/even mix, spread and letter, never their exact numbers. The pattern also counts 2 imaginary average jackpots, so one jackpot cannot swing it on its own.
explanation.dates: 7 jackpot dates. Calendar peaks - moon phase: about 2 days before the full moon; day of month: around the 23rd; weekday: none. None of these is clear after allowing for the 3 checks, so they may well be chance; if real, it would most likely be a ticket-sales effect. The balls do not know the date.
explanation.daily: 205 daily draws since 27 Mar 2026, without the 3 jackpot draws, turned down to 9% of their pull.
explanation.sets: Top pick: the ticket that follows all the evidence most closely, keeping the order jackpot combinations, then jackpot dates, then daily draws. Jackpot pattern, Jackpot days and Daily draws: each the ticket that follows its own source most closely. Lucky dip: a random ticket that follows the same pick rules. No two cards share more than 2 numbers. Each card shares at most 1 number with any one past jackpot and at most 2 with all of them, and no card repeats a past result.
explanation.backtest: Replayed over the last 178 draws, using only what was known before each draw: 0.163 numbers per draw; a random ticket matches 0.195. That is the same as random; the difference is luck. Across all 5 lotteries (934 draws): 0.1863 vs 0.2042.
explanation.odds: Every ticket has the same chance: 1 in 1,749,060 for the four numbers (1 in 45,475,560 with the letter).
explanation.limits: No method can foresee a random draw. Jackpot data describes the players, not the machine. For fun only.

notes: While jackpot combinations are known, the Top pick's letter is always the letter of a past jackpot. Letters are drawn separately from the numbers, so this repeats no combination.
Sunday Bonus digits are not predicted.
